question: A spherical tank has a diameter of 10 metres. What is the volume of the spherical tank? (Use π = 3.141)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The diameter of the sphere is 10 m, so the radius is 5 m.

Volume of a sphere = ⁴⁄₃ × π × r³

Volume = ⁴⁄₃ × 3.141 × 5³ = ⁴⁄₃ × 3.141 × 125

Volume = ¹⁵⁷⁰.⁵⁄₃ = 523.5 m³.

**∴ The correct answer is 523.5 cubic metre.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter of the spherical tank (d) = 10 m

Value of π = 3.141

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a sphere = ⁴⁄₃ × π × r³

where r is the radius of the sphere (r = d ÷ 2).

 
 

 

 
 
 
 
• 
 r = 5 m
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Diameter = 10 m
 
 
• 
 
• 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Radius (r) = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 m

⇒ Volume = ⁴⁄₃ × 3.141 × (5)³

⇒ Volume = ⁴⁄₃ × 3.141 × 125

⇒ Volume = ⁽⁴ × ¹²⁵⁾⁄₃ × 3.141

⇒ Volume = ⁵⁰⁰⁄₃ × 3.141

⇒ Volume = 1570.5 ÷ 3

⇒ Volume = 523.5 m³

**∴ The correct answer is 523.5 cubic metre.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Surface Area of a Sphere

The total surface area of a sphere is given by the formula 4 × π × r². A sphere has only one continuous curved surface, so its total and curved surface areas are the same.

Volume of a Hemisphere

A hemisphere is exactly half of a full sphere. Its volume is calculated as ²⁄₃ × π × r³.

Surface Area of a Hemisphere

The curved surface area of a solid hemisphere is 2 × π × r². If the circular base is included, the total surface area becomes 3 × π × r².
